title: ¿Quién es? and Es
explanation: Use ¿Quién es? to ask who a person is. Use es to identify another person. This is third-person use, not self-introduction.

title: Se llama
explanation: Use se llama to say another person’s name. Use me llamo for yourself and te llamas when asking you.

title: mi and tu with roles
explanation: Use mi for my and tu for your. In this module, keep roles short: mi amigo, mi amiga, tu profesor.

title: Basic role and adjective agreement
explanation: Some role and description words change final -o to -a for feminine forms. This module teaches only common pairs used in the lessons.

title: ¿Cómo es?
explanation: Use ¿Cómo es? to ask what a person is like. Answer with es plus one short description.

title: Third-person identity facts
explanation: Use es, vive and habla for another person. Contrast with soy/vivo/hablo for yourself and eres/vives/hablas for you.
examples: Soy de Ucrania. / Es de Ucrania.
Vivo en Kyiv. / Vive en Kyiv.

title: Yes/no questions about a person
explanation: Use ¿Es...? or ¿Habla...? to ask a yes/no question about another person. Answer sí or no without changing the facts.
examples: ¿Es tu amigo? Sí, es mi amigo.

title: Short conversation about another person
explanation: A short everyday conversation can identify a person, give a role, and add one origin, residence or language fact.
examples: Es mi amiga. Se llama Marta.
